# 1-Day SVN → Git Migration Plan

## Prerequisites (Night Before)
- [ ] Install `git-svn` or `svn2git`
- [ ] Notify team: SVN is read-only starting migration day
- [ ] Back up SVN repo
- [ ] Collect author list from SVN

---

## Morning (2–3 hrs): Prep & Convert

### 1. Freeze SVN (9:00 AM)
```bash
# Set repo to read-only or notify team to stop committing
```

### 2. Build Authors File (9:15 AM)
```bash
svn log https://svn-repo/project -q | \
  awk '/^r/ {print $3}' | sort -u | \
  sed 's/\(.*\)/\1 = Full Name <email@example.com>/' > authors.txt
# Edit authors.txt manually to fill in real names/emails
```

### 3. Clone SVN → Git (9:30 AM)
```bash
git svn clone https://svn-repo/project \
  --authors-file=authors.txt \
  --no-metadata \          # omit git-svn-id lines
  --stdlayout \            # assumes trunk/branches/tags
  -s \
  my-project-git
```
> ⏱ Runtime: minutes to hours depending on repo size/history

---

## Midday (1–2 hrs): Clean Up

### 4. Convert Tags & Branches (11:00 AM)
```bash
cd my-project-git

# Convert remote branches to local
git for-each-ref refs/remotes/origin/tags | \
  cut -d/ -f5- | while read tag; do
    git tag "$tag" "refs/remotes/origin/tags/$tag"
    git branch -r -d "origin/tags/$tag"
  done

# Convert remaining remote branches to local
git for-each-ref refs/remotes | \
  cut -d/ -f4- | grep -v HEAD | while read branch; do
    git branch "$branch" "refs/remotes/$branch"
    git branch -r -d "$branch"
  done
```

### 5. Verify History (11:30 AM)
```bash
git log --oneline | head -20
git branch -a
git tag
```

---

## Early Afternoon (1 hr): Push to Remote

### 6. Create Remote Repo (12:30 PM)
- Create empty repo on GitHub / GitLab / Bitbucket

### 7. Push Everything (12:45 PM)
```bash
git remote add origin https://github.com/org/my-project.git
git push origin --all
git push origin --tags
```

---

## Late Afternoon (2 hrs): Team Onboarding

### 8. Each Developer Runs (2:00 PM)
```bash
git clone https://github.com/org/my-project.git
```

### 9. Update CI/CD & Tooling (2:30 PM)
- [ ] Update pipeline repo URLs
- [ ] Update webhooks/integrations
- [ ] Update README badges/links
- [ ] Disable/archive SVN repo

### 10. Smoke Test (3:30 PM)
- [ ] Open a test PR/MR
- [ ] Verify CI passes
- [ ] Confirm team can push/pull

---

## Rollback Plan
> If something goes wrong before 2 PM → re-enable SVN, reschedule

---

## Quick Reference: Tool Choice

| Tool | Best For |
|------|----------|
| `git svn` | Built-in, simple repos |
| `svn2git` | Cleaner tag/branch handling |
| `reposurgeon` | Complex history surgery |

## Top 3 Migration Risks

### 1. 🧑‍💻 Commits During Migration
**Risk:** Someone commits to SVN after freeze, changes are lost.
**Mitigation:** Hard read-only lock on SVN repo, not just a verbal agreement.

---

### 2. 👤 Incomplete Authors File
**Risk:** Unknown SVN usernames cause conversion to fail or produce garbage author data in Git history.
**Mitigation:** Audit `authors.txt` completely before running clone — add `--authors-prog` fallback for unknowns.

---

### 3. 🌿 Mangled Branches/Tags
**Risk:** Non-standard SVN layouts (e.g., nested branches, multiple trunk copies) convert incorrectly or are silently dropped.
**Mitigation:** Audit `git branch -a` and `git tag` output against SVN before pushing; spot-check commit counts per branch.

## Migration Checklist

**Before**
- [ ] Back up SVN repo
- [ ] Freeze SVN (read-only)
- [ ] Complete `authors.txt`

**During**
- [ ] Verify branch/tag count matches SVN
- [ ] Spot-check commit history

**After**
- [ ] Push all branches and tags
- [ ] Update CI/CD URLs
- [ ] Archive SVN repo
- [ ] Team confirms clone + push works
Re-enable SVN read/write access — since you froze it (not deleted it), it remains a full fallback until you're confident the Git migration is verified.
`git-svn` must be installed before migration day.

user_text: What is the fastest validation step?
assistant_text: Run `git log --oneline | head -20` and confirm the most recent commits match SVN's last known commits.
Freeze SVN → Convert → Clean up → Push → Onboard team → Archive SVN (all within one business day).

State who should approve the final cutover.
assistant_text: The team lead or project owner.
Send a calendar invite to the whole team marking the exact SVN freeze time so no one commits at the wrong moment.

## Final Recap

Freeze SVN, convert history with `git svn` or `svn2git`, clean up branches/tags, push to remote, update CI/CD, and archive SVN — all in one day. Key risks are rogue commits, bad author data, and mangled branches. Team lead approves cutover, and everyone confirms clone + push works before SVN is retired.

- Freeze SVN first
- Convert with `git svn` or `svn2git`
- Clean up branches and tags
- Verify history matches
- Push all branches and tags
- Update CI/CD URLs
- Team lead approves cutover
- Team confirms clone + push
- Archive SVN
